title: Little Dumbbell Nebula (WFC3 Image)
caption: The Little Dumbbell Nebula (M76), imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Little Dumbbell Nebula, M76 · constellation Perseus · about 3,400 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: NASA Hubble image release (STScI). No published audience rating.

story: Two translucent lobes, mottled with blue, red and orange gas, spread from a thick white band at the centre of the Little Dumbbell Nebula. Catalogued as Messier 76, the nebula lies 3,400 light-years away in Perseus, a northern circumpolar constellation, and Hubble photographed it to mark the 34th anniversary of its launch.

M76 is a planetary nebula, a shell of glowing gas thrown off by a dying red giant star. The white band is a ring of gas and dust seen edge-on, probably shaped by a companion star that the central star may later have swallowed. The star itself is collapsing into a white dwarf, one of the hottest stellar remnants known at 250,000 degrees Fahrenheit, and shows as a pinpoint at the centre.

Two lobes of hot gas escape above and below the ring, driven at two million miles per hour by the outflow from the dying star. Its ultraviolet light makes the gas glow, red from nitrogen and blue from oxygen. The nebula will vanish in about 15,000 years.
scale: NASA lists this view as about 5 arcminutes across, roughly about 5 light-years at the object’s distance.

understand.summary: A composite from Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3. F475W is shown in cyan, F502N in blue, F656N in green, F658N in red and F814W in orange.
understand.eye: Narrow filters single out the glow of individual gases such as nitrogen and oxygen, and the F814W filter reaches into near-infrared light beyond what the eye sees well.

behind.people: See full credit: NASA, ESA, STScI
behind.exposure: Observation dates per NASA: 21 Jan - 23 Jan 2024.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: Planetary nebulae have nothing to do with planets. Astronomers in the 1700s, using low-power telescopes, thought such objects looked like planets, and the name stuck. A star that appears just below the white dwarf is not part of the nebula and only lies along the same line of sight.
sources: NASA release: Hubble Celebrates 34th Anniversary with a Look at the Little Dumbbell Nebula
alt: A nebula of two translucent, multicoloured lobes joined by a thick white band, surrounded by gold-coloured stars.
